old.name: Plaka
old.teaser: The oldest quarter, the most touristed marble in Greece.
old.text: The oldest continuously inhabited quarter, the 'neighbourhood of the gods' against the Acropolis's north-east flank, and the most touristed square kilometre in Greece. Walk it for the stacked layers — the white island-style lanes of Anafiotika climbing the rock — not for the dinner. Best at 07:00–09:00 before the cruise coaches, or a rainy winter evening when it empties and turns local again.
old.meta: BEST — 07:00–09:00, or a rainy winter evening

old.name: Monastiraki
old.teaser: The bazaar crossroads since Ottoman times.
old.text: The bazaar crossroads since Ottoman times, named for the 10th-century Pantanassa monastery on the square. One sightline holds the Tzistarakis mosque of 1759 and the wall of Hadrian's Library. Come Sunday from 08:00 for the Yusurum flea market along Avissynias; a weekday late afternoon for the square's light and the trains rattling under Hadrian's wall.
old.meta: BEST — Sunday from 08:00; weekday late afternoon

old.name: Psyrri
old.teaser: Hammers by day, rebetiko by night, street art overhead.
old.text: The artisans' quarter — leather, sandals, wicker, tin — that 1990s policy rebranded as the nightlife district. Hammers still sound by day; live rebetiko carries after dark, under some of the densest street art in Europe. Come weekday mornings for the surviving workshops, Friday–Saturday after 22:00 for the rebetiko cellars.
old.meta: BEST — weekday mornings; Fri–Sat after 22:00

old.name: Exarcheia
old.teaser: The students'-anarchists' quarter, the city's best bookshops.
old.text: The publishers'-students'-anarchists' quarter behind the Polytechnic, ground zero of the 1973 uprising. Its square has been fenced off since August 2022 for a Line 4 metro station; its bookshops and radical presses remain the city's best. Come Saturday 07:00–13:00 for the Kallidromiou laiki, weeknights for ouzo and vinyl.
old.meta: BEST — Saturday 07:00–13:00; weeknights

old.name: Metaxourgeio / Kerameikos
old.teaser: Silk-mill ruins, pioneer galleries, an ancient cemetery.
old.text: Named for the 19th-century silk mill on Avdi Square — ex-industrial, ex-red-light, now the city's most interesting collision. Chinese wholesalers and pioneer galleries (Rebecca Camhi has shown here since 1995), koutoukia beside experimental stages, the ancient Kerameikos cemetery beyond. Come after 20:00, Avdi Square on a summer evening; Monday morning for the Kerameikos street laiki.
old.meta: BEST — after 20:00; Monday morning for the laiki

old.name: Kolonaki
old.teaser: Old-money slope of Lycabettus, the city's polished salon.
old.text: The old-money slope of Lycabettus, named for a medieval column found at Dexameni. Embassies, tailors, the Benaki and Cycladic museums, a serious gallery circuit — the city's polished salon, not a cooking quarter. Come at weekday aperitivo hour on Dexameni Square; summer nights at the open-air cinema above it.
old.meta: BEST — weekday aperitivo hour; summer cinema nights

old.name: Pangrati
old.teaser: Pound for pound the most food-serious neighbourhood in Athens.
old.text: The middle-class quarter behind the Kallimarmaro stadium, home turf of composer Hatzidakis and the poet Seferis, and pound for pound the most food-serious neighbourhood in Athens. Its life runs between Plateia Proskopon and the newer Plateia Varnava. Come in the evening — vermouth on Varnava, then dinner; book ahead Thursday–Saturday.
old.meta: BEST — evenings; book ahead Thursday–Saturday

old.name: Koukaki
old.teaser: Airbnb ground zero below Filopappou, café strips intact.
old.text: A working-class grid below Filopappou hill that became Athens's Airbnb ground zero — a June 2025 ProtoThema investigation reckoned 60–70% of its long-term renters displaced. The café strips on Olympiou and Drakou still hold; the Acropolis Museum sits at its edge without Plaka pricing. Come weekday mornings for coffee; weekend evenings run fullest with the rental tide.
old.meta: BEST — weekday mornings; avoid the fullest weekend evenings

old.name: Ano Petralona
old.teaser: The closest central Athens comes to a prewar village.
old.text: The strip between the old ISAP tracks and Filopappou hill, the closest central Athens comes to a prewar village — pastel houses under bitter-orange trees and the densest run of honest tavernas in the centre, along Troon and around Merkouri Square. Come on summer nights when the tables spill onto Troon; Sunday lunch belongs to the families.
old.meta: BEST — summer nights on Troon; Sunday family lunch

old.name: Kypseli
old.teaser: A 1930s bourgeois quarter in the city's most watched revival.
old.text: A 1930s–60s bourgeois quarter, once among the most densely populated in Europe, now the city's most watched revival. Its spine is the green Fokionos Negri promenade, where Ghanaian barbershops, Art Deco lobbies and third-wave roasters share a pavement, anchored by the restored Municipal Market. Come at late-afternoon volta on Fokionos Negri; Saturday morning around the market.
old.meta: BEST — late-afternoon volta; Saturday market morning

old.name: The Pikionis Paths of Philopappou
old.teaser: A hand-laid marble path to the Acropolis, improvised stone by stone in the 1950s.
old.text: Between 1954 and 1957 Dimitris Pikionis, professor at the NTUA, paved the approach to Philopappou by hand — setting salvaged marble and clay from demolished neoclassical Athens into a collage where no two metres repeat, refusing finished drawings, directing his students stone by stone on site. In 1996 the Ministry of Culture listed the footpath itself as a protected monument. The Parthenon appears and vanishes between the pines at angles he composed. Flat rubber soles only — the marble turns lethal in rain; no fountain up top, so carry water.
old.meta: START opposite the Dionysiou Areopagitou–Apostolou Pavlou junction · free · unlit after dark, flat rubber soles only

old.name: Dionysiou Areopagitou — the Grand Promenade
old.teaser: The pedestrian marble avenue under the whole Acropolis south slope.
old.text: Until 2001 this was a car park at the foot of the rock; the Unification of Archaeological Sites programme pedestrianized it in 2001–2003, just before the 2004 Olympics, stitching the Theatre of Dionysus, the Odeon of Herodes Atticus (AD 161), Philopappou and the Agora into one marble line. It is named for Dionysius the Areopagite, the judge converted by Saint Paul, who preached on the Areopagus rock at its far end. Walk it at dusk when the Herodeon and Parthenon walls light; no shade at midday in July–August.
old.meta: START beside the Acropolis Museum, into Apostolou Pavlou toward Thiseio · free · no midday shade

old.name: Anafiotika at Dawn
old.teaser: A Cycladic hamlet of whitewashed cubes, built overnight on the Acropolis rock.
old.text: In 1841 builders from the barren island of Anafi, summoned to raise King Otto's capital, found no housing and built their own on the Acropolis rock overnight — invoking the Ottoman custom that a house roofed between sunset and sunrise could stand, and ignoring the 1834 decree that made the slope an archaeological zone. Roughly 45 whitewashed houses survive, still lived in, jasmine over blue doors. Come at dawn: it is residential, so whisper; the lanes are dead-ends that double back, which is the point.
old.meta: START above Stratonos street via the Agios Georgios tou Vrachou chapel · free · residential, whisper

old.name: Kerameikos to Gazi
old.teaser: The potters' quarter and cemetery, then the gasworks reborn as Technopolis, 400 m on.
old.text: The word 'ceramic' starts here — the potters' quarter on the clay banks of the Eridanos, which doubled as the city's cemetery from the Bronze Age, its grandest gate opening onto the Sacred Way to Eleusis. It is the quietest great ruin in Athens; walk it in the last two hours before closing, then cross 400 metres to Gazi, where the municipal gasworks lit the streets from 1857 to August 1984 and reopened in 1999 as Technopolis. The bulls and sphinxes on site are casts; the originals sit in museums.
old.meta: START Kerameikos site, Ermou 148, Thiseio · site ticketed (Acropolis combined valid) · hours shorten off-season

walks:Kaisariani Monastery & the Hymettu.group: Out to the pines and the sea

old.group: Out to the pines and the sea
old.name: Kaisariani Monastery & the Hymettus Pines
old.teaser: An 11th-century monastery in a pine fold of Hymettus, thirty minutes from Syntagma.
old.text: Sacred ground three times over — an ancient shrine of Aphrodite, then the late-11th-century Byzantine monastery raised over an earlier church, whose monks worked vines and hives until the house emptied in 1833. Hymettus honey was the classical world's benchmark, and the hillside still smells of it: wild thyme and sage crush underfoot, cold water runs by the courtyard fountain, bees everywhere, and the replanted Kaisariani Aesthetic Forest holds the whole city to the sea. Closed Tuesdays, no café — carry water, and budget a taxi up.
old.meta: START Kaisariani Monastery, NW foot of Hymettus · free forest, small monastery fee · closed Tue, modest dress

walks:Athens Riviera: Flisvos to Edem.group: Out to the pines and the sea

old.group: Out to the pines and the sea
old.name: Athens Riviera: Flisvos to Edem
old.teaser: Five flat kilometres of seafront, from a 1911 battleship to a mega-yacht marina.
old.text: The armoured cruiser Georgios Averof — bought in 1909 with a third of its namesake benefactor's estate, flagship at Elli (1912) and Lemnos (1913), a floating museum since 1984 — rides at the Trocadero jetty. From there the seafront runs unbroken past Flisvos Marina's 310 berths, hulls to 110 metres, to Edem beach at Kalamaki, with the tram back. Shadeless between the parks, so take a hat and water in summer; the Averof closes earlier than the walk needs, so board it first.
old.meta: START Trocadero jetty, Palaio Faliro · free (small fee for the Averof ship) · tram back from Edem

old.name: Edem Beach
old.teaser: The tram stops at the sand — the city's own free swim
old.text: Edem is where the city itself swims: the beach is a tram stop, and Palaio Faliro treats the sand as a public square with water. The water is honest city water — swimmable, officially a beach, no Blue Flag, not the clearest on the coast. That is the point. Half an hour from Syntagma, free, and no journey required, which is exactly why the city loves it.
old.meta: FREE · Tram T6→T7 to the Edem stop, 25-35 min from Syntagma

old.name: Megalo Kavouri
old.teaser: The best free sand within the hour, over a drowned ancient road
old.text: A ~900 m run of free sand with pines at its back, facing west, so the sun drops into the water in front of you. The municipality's own listing notes the oddity: an ancient submerged road shows through the shallows, and you can wade the drowned causeway on foot to the islet off the point — older than the suburb behind you. The name means 'crab'. Families hold the shallow middle; the rocky ends belong to snorkellers.
old.meta: FREE · M2 to Elliniko + bus 122 to the Kavouri stops, 60-75 min · parking scarce summer weekends

calas:Akti Vouliagmenis.group: Paid for — and what you get

old.name: Akti Vouliagmenis
old.teaser: Blue Flag water and a ten-euro sunbed — the fair middle rung
old.text: The reliable middle rung of the ladder: Blue Flag 2026, big, shallow, family-proof. A sunbed runs EUR 10 on a weekday, 15 at the weekend — the sane price between free Kavouri and the gate at Astir, over the same Saronic blue. Weekends heave in July and August; go on a weekday, or in September when the water is warmest and the schools are back.
old.meta: €10 wkday / €15 wknd (2026) · Blue Flag · M2 + bus 122 to Plaz Vouliagmenis, 65-75 min

calas:Astir Beach.group: Paid for — and what you get

old.name: Astir Beach
old.teaser: Athens' priciest cove buys patina, not clearer water
old.text: Athens' most expensive swim — EUR 50 on a weekday, 80 at the weekend — buys sixty-five years of patina, not better water. It opened in 1959 on monastery land at Laimos for Onassis, Bardot and Sinatra; the seagull-wing shades are still the emblem. The hotel above reopened in 2019 as the Four Seasons Astir Palace. The connoisseur move: a EUR 10 winter-weekday ticket puts you in the same cove in low light.
old.meta: €50 wkday / €80 wknd (May-Sep 2026); winter €10/15 · book at tickets.astir.gr · taxi ~35 min

old.name: Limanakia (Cove B)
old.teaser: No sand, no lifeguard — the clearest water within 25 km
old.text: No sand, no lifeguard, no toilets — nothing sold but canteen beer, and the clearest water within 25 km of Syntagma, paid for in scraped knees. Since at least the 1970s the Limanakia have been the city's free bohemian shore; cove B is Athens' best-known queer swimming spot, which the official Athens guide now celebrates. Water shoes essential; the 'Devil's Well', an 11 m freediving hole off a red buoy, carries a real accident history. Go as a respectful guest.
old.meta: FREE · no lifeguard, no infrastructure · M2 + bus 122 to the Limanakia stops, ~30 min · water shoes essential

old.name: Lake Vouliagmeni
old.teaser: A warm brackish spring you can swim in January
old.text: The only swim in Attica that works in January without a wetsuit: 22-24C brackish spring water in the collapsed roof of a thermal cave, sea-connected and spring-fed. Cave divers are still mapping the drowned galleries beneath it. The fish pedicure the spas charge for is free and wild here — endemic Garra rufa 'doctor fish' nibble your feet in the shallows. EUR 17 on a 2026 weekday; the free sea sits 300 m across the road.
old.meta: €17 wkday / €19 wknd (2026) · year-round, daily · M2 + bus 122 to Plaz Vouliagmenis + 10-min walk, 70-80 min
